# Five Dividend-paying Transport Stocks to Buy


By:[Paul Dykewicz](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/author/pdykewicz-admin/)


, September 25, 2026


Link copied!


Five dividend-paying[transport stocks](https://www.stockinvestor.com/three-transport-stocks-to-buy-in-benefitting-from-ai/) to buy feature railroads, trucking companies and overnight delivery services.


The five dividend-paying transport stocks are gaining buy recommendations amid the continuing conflict in the Middle East that has hampered shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. All of the companies have a strong North American focus in a part of the world that is not engaging in military clashes.


The Intermodal Association of North America (IANA) held its Intermodal Expo 2026 at the Long Beach, California, Convention Center, Sept. 14-16. The event focused on two key points: 1) Intermodal is having a moment, as industry participants discussed how to capitalize on the best growth prospects in years; and 2) Speculation is circulating about the potential impacts of the proposed $85 billion merger between[Union Pacific](https://www.up.com/press-releases/growth/stb-rejects-dismissal-request-260922) Corp. (NYSE: UNP) and Norfolk Southern Corp. (NYSE: NSC), which aims to create America’s first single-line transcontinental railroad, wrote Citi Research.


“We noted considerable optimism at the IANA Conference, as the combination of elevated fuel prices, tight trucking capacity, record global container volumes and resilient consumer spending is creating some of the best conditions in years for intermodal to win share,” Citi Research wrote in a recent research note.


Several railroad companies are posting record high intermodal volumes, while UNP is close behind, posting double-digit-percentage year-over-year intermodal carload growth for third quarter into September 2026, Citi Research continued.


Globally, 95% of all manufactured goods at one point are moved in a container, according to the IANA. It shows that continuing economic growth should give transport companies a boost.


**Five Dividend-paying Transport Stocks to Buy: Fed Factor**


The Fed Reserve raised the benchmark federal funds rate last week by 25 basis points, and market veteran Jim Woods wrote in the just-completed October issue of *[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS)* that he was among those not surprised. The markets had priced that move in, as there was a 92% chance of a rate hike per CME FedWatch the day before the hike, he wrote.


“Yet what the market really wanted to see was the so-called ‘dot plot,’ which is where the members of the FOMC think rates will be in the future,” Woods wrote. “Those dots revealed that 16 of 18 Fed officials think there will be one more rate hike before the end of the year.”


*Jim Woods is rated as the No. 1 stock blogger by Tip Ranks.*


This is what market watchers like me were calling a “one or two and done” Fed policy move, as in one or two rate hikes before year-end to both establish the Fed’s credibility as inflation fighters, and to notify markets that the Fed and Warsh are, in fact, independent entities that will not kowtow to the White House, commented Woods, who also leads advisory services[Bullseye Stock Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/bullseye-default/?source=GURUBEST1) ,[Five Star Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/five-star-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUFST) ,[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=DWDEF1) and[TNT Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tnt-trader-web-default-2/?source=DWDEF1) that offer stock and option recommendations.

**Five Dividend-paying Transport Stocks to Buy: UNP**


Union Pacific’s Chief Executive Officer Jim Vena told attendees at the event that ultimately it would be up to customers to decide if the merger was beneficial, but argued that if the STB rejects the merger, it would effectively be choosing to keep supply chains less efficient, wrote Citi Research. The CEO also highlighted UNP’s efficiency gains in recent years, noting that the company would need 25% more trains if it were still operating at the same levels of productivity that it was at in 2019, the investment firm wrote.


In addition, Omaha, Nebraska’s Union Pacific has reported “velocity metrics” at roughly 230 miles per day, up significantly from recent years, with these benefits creating ways for the railroad to be less expensive, even with all the pressures of inflation, while opening up capacity without spending more on capital, Citi Research wrote. Alternatively, critics have noted that it will be difficult for shippers and regulators to hold UNP accountable for its claimed benefits post-merger, the investment firm continued.


Citi Research rates Union Pacific as a buy but noted the its share price has climbed into a “fair value” range. However, it also is “hard” to discount macro tailwinds, the investment firm added.


Income investors may appreciate that Union Pacific’s current annual dividend yield is a tad above 2.0%.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://stockcharts.com/) .*


**Five Dividend-paying Transport Stocks to Buy: CP**


Canadian Pacific Kansas City Ltd. (TSE: CP) has a forward dividend yield of 0.87%, so it is on the low side compared to others that pay dividends to their shareholders. The Canadian-based company, headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, is traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange but remains a Citi Research buy recommendation.


Citi Research recently wrote that it continues to see upside in CP on its synergy tailwind and expected second-half 2026 volume “inflection” driving operating leverage. The railroad holds the distinction of operating as the first and only single-line transnational freight railway connecting Canada, the United States and Mexico.


BNSF Railway Chief Executive Officer Katie Farmer recently said that the merger that considated CP has not produced the kinds of results projected by its management. CP made commitments to keep gateways open prior to its merger, but that BNSF used to move “thousands of units” across the Laredo route in Mexico, and that has now fallen to zero post-merger with the gateway effectively closed to other railroads despite being nominally open, she added.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://stockcharts.com/) .*


**Five Dividend-paying Transport Stocks to Buy: UPS**


Atlanta-based UPS (NYSE: UPS), wrote Citi Research in a recent research note, is rated as a buy with a price target of $132. Even though UPS’s share price has fallen 5.1% so far in 2026 through Sept. 22, Citi Research recently wrote positively about the company and added that investors could be rewarded for their faith in the business. Citi Research analysts recently met with the UPS Chief Financial Officer Brian Dykes, who described a generally constructive operating environment, with volume and parcel demand that has been moderately better-than-expected given a resilient U.S. consumer and improving business-to-business activity.


Despite a “rational pricing environment,” UPS’s extensive cost cutting and efficiency efforts that are starting to be reflected in margin stabilization with gradual improvement expected into 2027, the company continues to face a “skeptical investor base,” given rolling challenges such as tariffs, risks from Amazon (NYSE: AMZN) and union strife, Citi Research wrote.


Advertisement.


“UPS sees these challenges largely subsiding, and while it acknowledged further risks from a wage step-up in ’27 and labor renegotiations in ‘28, it expressed confidence in its ability to manage these issues,” Citi Research wrote. “We believe UPS’s depressed valuation more than compensates for these uncertainties, offering a compelling risk-reward.”


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Five Dividend-paying Transport Stocks to Buy: JBHT**


“When I think about AI, it’s certainly a monumental change that is happening in front of us,” J. B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. (NASDAQ: JBHT) President and CEO Shelley Simpson told Business Roundtable attendees at a recent conference in Washington, D.C., that focused on AI. “But it’s not unusual for change in the last 32 years of my career.”


The company’s founder, J. B. Hunt, started operations with five trucks and seven trailers 65 years ago, and it has grown to become multi-modal across the supply chain in North America, Simpson said. That change alone has been significant as the company has entered into intra-modal transportation trucks, trains and now going into customers’ homes, she added.


In 2017, J. B. Hunt entered into a cycle of innovation that aimed to disrupt, adapt and accelerate change to meet the company’s changing business requirements. The company brought digital transformation into its business by investing $500 million in technology. In 2022, the company focused on its foundations of people, technology and capacity, she added.


Technology “empowers,” Simpson said. Employees can focus their “mindset” on ways to use technology to help with their work, she added.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Five Dividend-paying Transport Stocks to Buy: ODFL**


A third recommendation is Old Dominion Freight Line Inc (NASDAQ: ODFL). Woods recommended it an advisory service from December 13, 2022, to January 24, 2023, producing a 10.27% profit in the stock and a 72.48% gain in the calls. He is not currently recommending the freight train operator but watches the industry closely.


ODFL was among several freight operators that provided solid mid-quarter updates in the third quarter among key operating metrics in August, suggesting continued improvement in industry-wide supply/demand balance, according to Citi Research. The investment firm upgraded ODFL a “buy” following its recent share-price pullback, as it ranks as a leader in its transport sub-sector. The stock currently offers an opportunity to buy “quality” at a reasonable price, Citi Research wrote.


The freight operator is among the companies that has had its ups and downs but is forecasting improvement. Investors who agree may find the reduced stock price appealing.
